formex — development status, gaps & the test-data library

Status snapshot, 2026-10-25. A companion to the user-facing Type Atlas vignette (vignettes/formex-type-atlas.Rmd). The Atlas describes what each type is; this note records what is built, what is not, and what the detectors were tested against. Numbers are from the shipped ontology (fx_ontology(), 96 variants) and the dev test library (dev/feature_matrix_all.rds, 4,036 columns). The dev/ tree is local scaffolding and is not shipped or version-controlled, so the library figures are a point-in-time measurement, not a build artifact.

1. Where the engine stands

The two public verbs are both wired and pass the suite (121 tests, 0 failures):

  • guess_data_type() — two-stage router → verifier, returning the $route record plus the legacy fields.
  • fx_stabilize() — the transform executor (fx_transform() + a verb library) that the original integration plan listed as the critical missing path. It is now built; the DSL parser and ~31 verbs run against the ontology recipes.

Still per the plan and not formex’s to build: the datagoodr governance-file schema and the actual extraction of the moved files out of datagoodr (see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md).

2. Implementation coverage (what has a working detector)

Of 97 ontology variants, 48 (49%) are marked implemented = "yes" — a wired, exercised detector. The rest are declared recipes (data_format / transform / stable_format / import_rule are populated) waiting on a detector, verb, or gazetteer.

v7 session update. Coverage rose 36 → 46 by wiring test-backed, foil-selective detectors (data-raw/wire_detectors_v7.R): day_of_week / month_of_year (new as_dow / as_moy), first_name, quarter, domain, usd (new is_currency_amount — symbol-required), place (lookup:place), min_max range, and point / polygon (is_wkt_geometry, keyword-gated). Key finding worth carrying forward: a selective recipe is necessary but not sufficient to route — the learned router never shortlists very rare mask leaves (array, version, reporting_period confirm in isolation but never reach the verifier), so they stay unimplemented until either the router has training cases or they join the verifier’s always-on set (as the geometry family now does). Two verb bugs were fixed along the way: the DSL arg parser left a trailing ] on verb[arg], and as_range was loose enough to claim nested arrays as ranges.

Later in the session: the disambiguator landed (a disambiguator / collision_group column + a cardinality tie-break wired into the verifier, resolving the geographic grouping-vs-key and the cross-type place↔︎geographic collisions; fx_validate_ontology() fails on an undeclared collision). fx_stabilize() gained a conversion_log and a warning when present values are dropped to NA, so silent data loss is surfaced. From datagoodr’s dplyr::starwars report: a named-color leaf (text/color/color_name + is_color_name()) fixes color words leaking to geographic, and a write_numeric edge lets plain measurements stabilize to numeric; and a tags detector (is_tags) wires categorical/multiselect/tags for delimited list columns. Coverage is now 48/97; 92 detectors; 121 tests.

3. Unimplemented detectors, grouped

Highest leverage first (the mechanism tells you whether the work is a detector, a verb, or a reference list).

number — the biggest gap (0 of 23). Every quantity, portion, currency, range and coordinate variant is unimplemented. - shape (not subtype-detectable from values; need the header): measurement, count, rate, ratio, duration, score, index, rank, probability, odds, percent, percentile. - mask (detector + verb is real work): currency/{balance,usd,euro}, range/{comma_pair,to_range,confidence_interval}, coordinate/{lat_lon dms, lat_lon iso6709, lon_lat, lat, lon}.

boolean (0 of 5). is_boolean() exists and recognizes the two-state vocabulary, but no binary variant is marked implemented and the class (indicator / presence / status / response / mixed) needs the header. Worth reconciling: the detector is shipped but the ontology rows say otherwise.

structured (0 of 6). Detectors exist (is_json, is_wkt_geometry, is_geojson, is_wkb) but collection/{list,array}, record/{object, key_value} and geometry/{point,polygon} are not wired; recipes pass through as literal text.

temporal (6 of 12). Open: period/{quarter, reporting_period}, phase/{hour_of_day, day_of_week, month_of_year, week_of_year}.

text (14 of 24). Open: name/{first_name, last_name, full_name, place, handle} (lexicon-bound), text/{label, title, long, serialized} (none), web/domain.

categorical (7 of 13). Open: scale/{likert, rating, ranking, grade_level}, multiselect/tags, mutually_exclusive/missingness_reason — all none, i.e. codebook-gated.

identifier (9 of 10). Only id/version remains.

4. Repo hygiene gaps

  • Ontology drift. Resolved: the stale data-types/…_v6.csv duplicate was removed; fx_ontology() reads inst/extdata/ (the authority). (Older design snapshots …_v2/v3/v4.csv remain for history.)
  • No CI. Resolved: a standard r-lib R-CMD-check workflow (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) builds the package, runs the suite, and builds the vignettes on push / PR to main.
  • Version is still 0.0.0.9000; nothing published.
  • The benign NAs introduced by coercion to integer range warning fires ~18× across the suite (numeric-coercion paths) — cosmetic, worth bounding.

5. The test-data library

The detectors are measured against a unified library of 4,036 real and synthetic columns, one row per column, assembled from three sources and crosswalked to the formex ontology.

5.1 Columns ingested, by source

source columns nature
Sherlock / VizNet 3,423 real columns sampled from the ~137K-column VizNet test split; 78-type Sherlock label vocabulary. Labels derive from headers, so they are noisier — deliberately, as hard negatives
synthetic_temporal 436 generated columns across the temporal leaves, exact ground truth, an easy + mutated-hard mix, to give the router the dense, balanced temporal neighbourhood the wild corpora lack
GitTables 177 real columns with independent headers (so usable for the name-side evaluation too)
total 4,036

By formex data type the library leans heavily text/categorical/number:

text 1339 · categorical 1283 · number 667 · temporal 553 · identifier 149 · unknown 38 · structured 5 · boolean 2

5.2 How they were standardized into one library

A corpus-agnostic banking core (dev/bank_core.R) turns every source into the same shape, so everything downstream is identical regardless of origin:

  1. Record. Each source column becomes a record list(values, label, table_id, header) via a per-corpus adapter (GitTables CSV, Sherlock parquet, the temporal generator). Heterogeneous value encodings — stringified Python lists, Arrow list-columns, materialized vectors — are parsed to a clean character vector; headers are snake-cased.
  2. Crosswalk / resolve. A resolver maps the source’s own label vocabulary to a formex ontology coordinate through a *-crosswalk-v4.csv whose v4_type / v4_class / v4_subclass columns are the v6 path, emitting a semantic_type_id + variant_id against the live ontology.
  3. Triage & bank. fx_triage_field() → fx_make_test_case() writes a uniform schema-v2 JSON test case per column, with an exclusion log for rejects.
  4. Diversity sampling (Sherlock). 137K columns is too many and mostly redundant, so cases are chosen by farthest-point selection over fx_type_signature() distance (capped per type) rather than a random draw — maximizing shape diversity and surfacing hard negatives.
  5. Feature matrix. dev/build_feature_matrix.R assembles the labeled substrate the router/verifier train on: one row per banked column, the value-only v2 feature profile (~471 features) plus public-domain gazetteer membership features, joined to the label axes (data_type → variant_id). Result: feature_matrix_all.rds, 4,036 × 491.

5.3 Test cases per formex variant (after crosswalk)

Crosswalking to the ontology, 53 of 96 variants carry at least one test case; 43 carry none. Among variants that have cases: median 24, mean 73, max 611. The distribution is very uneven:

cases per variant 1 2–5 6–10 11–25 26–50 51–100 100+
variants 6 9 4 11 5 6 12

Best-covered variants:

variant cases path
n0044-f01 611 categorical / unordered
n0046-f01 459 categorical / iso_country
n0028-f01 371 text / organization
n0027-f01 359 text / first_name
n0001-f01 223 number / measurement
n0059-f01 182 temporal / calendar
n0002-f01 148 number / count
n0073-f01 77 identifier / ein

The coverage and the implementation status do not line up, which is the main testing gap:

  • 18 implemented variants have zero test cases — detectors with no independent column in the library to confirm them against.
  • 35 variants have test cases but are not implemented — labeled data waiting for a detector/verb (much of it the number/quantity and shape block, which the crosswalk can label but the engine cannot yet type by value).
  • Whole families are thin or empty: number/coordinate (3 cases), structured/geometry (1), boolean/binary (2), text/contact (2). Any accuracy claim there rests on a handful of columns.

5.4 Caveats

  • The library is banked against an earlier ontology snapshot (the build scripts reference a 92–94-row ontology); the crosswalk targets v6 paths, so labels resolve, but the 96-row shipped ontology has moved since.
  • dev/stabilize_rate.R — the source of the per-mechanism confirm rates — reads only the Sherlock + synthetic-temporal banks (feature_matrix.rds, 3,859 columns), not GitTables, and counts none / open-set types as not-stabilized.
  • Sherlock labels come from headers, so a slice of the “truth” is itself noisy; this is intentional (hard negatives) but caps the achievable top-1.
